current_mission: Use Tony's real student worksheet scans to make two-digit OCR trustworthy before expanding ScanGrade.
north_star: Primary students scan completed worksheets on shared iPads; teachers review saved results only when needed.
next_best_move: Codex: use the reproduced 5/10 subtraction scan plus the May 30 three-sheet benchmark as the gate for any narrow OCR/crop-preprocessing fix.
plain_english_status: We have the current Grade 2 worksheet packet published, the app/test path working, and real student handwriting evidence. Tony's newest subtraction scan reproduced a real OCR failure: the sheet and boxes are found, but thin pencil 2s and 7s are often read as 1 or 9, yielding 5/10 on that sheet. The May 30 benchmark remains 18/30 across three sheets. The next work should be evidence-based OCR diagnosis and narrow fixes only; Tony has locked the current app UI for now, so autonomous work should not make further app UI/style/layout changes unless he asks.
needs_tony: Send any additional completed Addition, Subtraction, or Mixed sheets as clear full-page photos when available.
Keep using normal student pencil/spacing; imperfect handwriting is the useful test.
If possible, note whether a scan was from the live app, a phone photo, or an iPad photo.
blocked_or_risky: Two-digit OCR is not yet classroom-trustworthy: newest subtraction sample scores 5/10 despite correct sheet detection.
OCR/capture/homography files contain large tracked modifications and should not be changed or pushed casually.
Debug crop export specs create local artifacts when run, so only run them intentionally.

cards.title: Diagnose failed subtraction scan
cards.summary: Tony's newest student scan is a reproducible two-digit OCR failure: 5/10 on Subtraction Within 20.
cards.detail: The app finds the sheet and answer boxes, but thin pencil 2s and 7s are degraded in the 28x28 model inputs and misread as 1 or 9. Use this sample with the May 30 benchmark before accepting any OCR change.

cards.title: Send more student sheets when convenient
cards.summary: More real completed A/B/C sheets will make OCR tuning less likely to overfit one student or one photo.
cards.detail: Good enough: full page visible, corners included, not badly blurred. Perfect lighting is not required.

cards.title: Gate any OCR fix against real samples
cards.summary: Any crop-preprocessing or candidate-selection fix must improve Tony's failed subtraction scan without reducing the May 30 benchmark.
cards.detail: Current baseline: newest subtraction sample 5/10; May 30 benchmark 18/30. Do not push OCR changes as improvements until they clear this gate.

cards.title: Do not tune OCR blind
cards.summary: OCR/capture changes should wait for real sample evidence or a reproducible failing test.
cards.detail: This protects the currently promising MacBook/upload behavior and avoids overfitting to imagined problems.

cards.title: Decide pilot threshold
cards.summary: After real samples are tested, decide what is good enough for a small classroom pilot.
cards.detail: This should be based on scan success rate, retry behavior, and teacher-review usefulness.

codex_autonomy_rule: Codex should keep moving every 15 minutes when useful: inspect repo state, choose the safest high-value work from the mission/kanban, and prefer small reversible packets. Safe autonomous lanes include tests, diagnosis, docs, Mission Control upkeep, worksheet/TPT/marketing drafts, market research, and careful planning. Tony has locked the current app UI for now, so do not make further app UI/style/layout changes autonomously. Tony remains final authority for vision, brand, major UX, launch/pricing/claims, worksheet-format decisions, and risky OCR/capture/homography/model/backend changes. Never delete/clean untracked work, never run git clean -fd or git reset --hard, and preserve paper-first teacher trust over feature expansion.
